maria: quick note: i prototyped a "permit token" gateway to run auth pre-fanout. it returns small signed tokens workers can cache. please review tradeoffs.

cheng: nice. how much latency does it add?

maria: local tests show ~3ms median, p99 +9ms on cold miss. with local LRU reuse it's ~1.5ms median.

owen: big Q: policy rollouts. if we push a deny, we must avoid stale tokens allowing access.

maria: plan A: short TTLs (200-1000ms) + publish invalidations. plan B: include policy_version in token and have workers revalidate on mismatch.

cheng: option B preferred for correctness. on mismatch worker hits gateway; rare but safe. add metric for revalidations.

owen: batch support? dashboards sometimes fan out to hundreds of shards.

maria: added /auth/batch; gateway supports bulk token responses and internal coalescing. reduces N x 1.

infra-bot: deploy: canary 7f2a passed basic smoke. gateway pod CPU ~8% under synthetic.

cheng: fallback behavior if gateway unavailable? deny-by-default is safe but painful. propose per-route fallback config (deny/allow-audit/degrade-with-cache).

maria: will add per-route config. sample: {"routes":{"dash.read":{"fallback":"deny","ttl_ms":500},"ping":{"fallback":"allow-audit","ttl_ms":2000}}}

owen: cache design: shared LRU with per-tenant soft quotas to limit noisy neighbors. track eviction counters.

maria: agreed. tasks: 1) add eviction + revalidation metrics 2) add e2e policy-rollout test in release pipeline 3) run tenancy loadbench for memory behavior 4) design KMS rotation for private deployments.

cheng: also add signature rotation plan and consider ed25519 for cross-cluster verification later.

maria: thanks team  thumbsup
